title: Families over the ring — 63 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Families over the ring. 63 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/families.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 42 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 21 are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). One further declaration closes by rfl, checked by evaluation, and is not included here, by design. Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 14 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 86 pairs; the theorems fall into 35 strands, the largest of 9. Most binding: powSum (8), choose (6), gcd' (6), primesUpTo30 (4), faulhaber (4), fib (4). 19 theorems name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: demand.lean, demand2.lean, elementary.lean. Checking this cluster needs 1 file: src/proof/families.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 63 sealed receipts fold to 5ebe59a9-4536-8224-97b7-4aeb617734b4. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (7, 4, 0, 8, 3, 0, 0). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: phenomena.lean (5 observed, 2.19 expected, lift 2.28), address.lean (26 observed, 13.68 expected, lift 1.9), fnv.lean (12 observed, 7.66 expected, lift 1.57). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 1.83 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 13.5% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.59; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.55. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 90fe8c570606 (2026-09-15), over 807 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Quantifies the ℤ/9 arithmetic above; the underlying results are Fermat’s, Euler’s and Gauss’s. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. flt_all_primes_under_thirty — primesUpTo30.all (fun p => (List.range' 1 (p - 1)).all (fun a => (a ^ (p - 1)) % p == 1)) record
  2. wilson_all_primes_under_thirty — primesUpTo30.all (fun p => fact (p - 1) % p == p - 1) record
  3. wilson_fails_at_composites — ((List.range' 4 20).filter (fun n => ! primesUpTo30.contains n)).all (fun n => fact (n - 1) % n != n - 1) record
  4. pascal_rows_sum_to_powers_of_two — (List.range 12).all (fun n => ((List.range (n + 1)).map (fun k => choose n k)).foldl (· + ·) 0 == 2 ^ n) record
  5. pascal_alternating_sums_vanish — (List.range' 1 11).all (fun n => ((List.range (n + 1)).map (fun k => if k % 2 == 0 then choose n k else 0)).foldl (· + ·) 0 == ((List.range (n + 1)).map (fun k => if k % 2 == 1 then choose n k else 0)).foldl (· + ·) 0) record
  6. totient_at_prime_powers — [2, 3, 5, 7].all (fun p => (List.range' 1 3).all (fun k => totient (p ^ k) == p ^ k - p ^ (k - 1))) record
  7. geometric_series_all_bases — (List.range' 2 8).all (fun b => ((List.range 5).map (fun i => b ^ i)).foldl (· + ·) 0 * (b - 1) == b ^ 5 - 1) record
  8. xor_is_parity_up_to_eight_bits — (List.range' 1 8).all (fun k => (List.range (2 ^ k)).all (fun n => popcount n % 2 == (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i => (acc + ((n >>> i) % 2)) % 2) 0)) record
  9. nat_div_is_a_total_function_returning_zero_at_a_zero_divisor — (7 / 0) = 0 ∧ (0 / 0) = 0 ∧ (7 % 0) = 7 record
  10. division_identity_holds_across_the_range — (List.range 13).all (fun d => (12 / d) * d + (12 % d) == 12) record
  11. at_a_zero_divisor_the_identity_is_carried_by_the_remainder — (12 / 0) = 0 ∧ (12 % 0) = 12 ∧ (12 / 0) * 0 + (12 % 0) == 12 record
  12. primality_is_decided_across_the_range — (List.range' 2 17).all (fun m => isPrime m == primesUpTo30.contains m) record
  13. the_units_are_cyclic_at_exactly_the_gauss_moduli — (List.range' 2 17).all (fun m => hasPrimitiveRoot m == gaussCyclic m) record
  14. demorgan_holds_at_every_arity_to_eight — (List.range' 2 7).all (fun k => (List.range (2 ^ k)).all (fun n => (! (List.range k).all (fun i => (n >>> i) % 2 == 1)) == (List.range k).any (fun i => (n >>> i) % 2 == 0))) record
  15. multiplication_permutes_z9_at_exactly_the_units — (List.range' 1 8).all (fun k => permutesZ9 k == (gcd' k 9 == 1)) record
  16. addition_generates_z9_at_exactly_the_units — (List.range' 1 8).all (fun k => addGeneratesZ9 k == (gcd' k 9 == 1)) record
  17. an_inverse_mod_nine_exists_at_exactly_the_units — (List.range 9).all (fun d => (invOf d).isSome == (gcd' d 9 == 1)) record
  18. the_inverse_of_a_unit_mod_nine_is_its_fifth_power — (unitsMod 9).all (fun u => u * (powMod u 5 9) % 9 == 1) record
  19. power_sums_match_their_closed_forms — (List.range' 1 5).all (fun k => (List.range 41).all (fun n => powSum k n == faulhaber k n)) record
  20. the_digital_root_is_invariant_under_digit_reversal — (List.range 100).all (fun a => (List.range 100).all (fun b => digitalRoot (a * 100 + b) == digitalRoot (reverseDigits (a * 100 + b)))) record
  21. geometric_series_across_bases_and_exponents — (List.range' 2 11).all (fun b => (List.range 7).all (fun n => ((List.range (n + 1)).map (fun i => b ^ i)).foldl (· + ·) 0 * (b - 1) == b ^ (n + 1) - 1)) record
  22. totient_at_prime_powers_through_thirteen — [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13].all (fun p => (List.range' 1 3).all (fun k => totient (p ^ k) == p ^ k - p ^ (k - 1))) record
  23. the_powers_of_a_unit_sum_to_zero_when_g_minus_one_is_invertible — (List.range' 2 19).all (fun m => (unitsMod m).all (fun g => !(gcd' (g - 1) m == 1) || (rootSum g m % m == 0))) record
  24. and_the_converse_fails_at_six — ordMod 5 6 = 2 ∧ rootSum 5 6 % 6 = 0 ∧ gcd' 4 6 = 2 record
  25. the_first_n_odd_numbers_sum_to_n_squared — (List.range 201).all (fun n => ((List.range n).map (fun i => 2 * i + 1)).foldl (· + ·) 0 == n * n) record
  26. the_powers_of_two_sum_to_one_less_than_the_next — (List.range 41).all (fun n => ((List.range (n + 1)).map (fun i => 2 ^ i)).foldl (· + ·) 0 == 2 ^ (n + 1) - 1) record
  27. the_sums_of_triangular_numbers_are_the_tetrahedral_numbers — (List.range 101).all (fun n => ((List.range' 1 n).map (fun i => i * (i + 1) / 2)).foldl (· + ·) 0 == n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) / 6) record
  28. the_squares_of_a_pascal_row_sum_to_the_central_binomial — (List.range 13).all (fun n => ((List.range (n + 1)).map (fun k => choose n k * choose n k)).foldl (· + ·) 0 == choose (2 * n) n) record
  29. polygonal_closed_forms_match_their_recurrences — (List.range' 3 8).all (fun s => (List.range 51).all (fun n => ((s - 2) * n * n + 4 * n - s * n) / 2 == polyRec s n)) record
  30. the_order_of_every_unit_mod_nine_divides_six — (unitsMod 9).all (fun u => ordMod u 9 > 0 && 6 % ordMod u 9 == 0 && powMod u (ordMod u 9) 9 == 1) record
  31. the_digit_square_iteration_reaches_one_or_four — (List.range' 1 200).all (fun n => iterF 60 n == 1 || iterF 60 n == 4) record
  32. a_number_is_a_sum_of_two_squares_exactly_when_fermats_condition_holds — (List.range' 1 200).all (fun n => isSumOfTwoSquares n == everyThreeModFourPrimeIsEven n) record
  33. the_first_three_power_sums_hold_to_two_hundred — (List.range' 1 3).all (fun k => (List.range 201).all (fun n => powSum k n == faulhaber k n)) record
  34. there_are_exactly_five_platonic_solids_and_each_satisfies_eulers_formula — schlafli.length = 5 ∧ schlafli.all (fun x => let d := 2 * x.1 + 2 * x.2 - x.1 * x.2 4 * x.1 % d == 0 && 2 * x.1 * x.2 % d == 0 && 4 * x.2 % d == 0 && 4 * x.1 / d + 4 * x.2 / d == 2 * x.1 * x.2 / d + 2) record
  35. cassinis_identity_holds_across_the_range — (List.range' 1 30).all (fun n => if n % 2 == 0 then fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) == fib n * fib n + 1 else fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) + 1 == fib n * fib n) record
  36. the_golden_convergents_are_fibonacci_ratios_with_unit_determinant — (List.range 25).all (fun n => (cfPair n).1 == fib (n + 2) && (cfPair n).2 == fib (n + 1) && (if n % 2 == 0 then (cfPair n).1 * (cfPair n).1 + 1 == (cfPair n).1 * (cfPair n).2 + (cfPair n).2 * (cfPair n).2 else (cfPair n).1 * (cfPair n).1 == (cfPair n).1 * (cfPair n).2 + (cfPair n).2 * (cfPair n).2 + 1)) record
  37. the_catalan_recurrence_matches_the_binomial_formula — (List.range 13).all (fun n => (catalanList 12).getD n 0 == choose (2 * n) n / (n + 1)) record
  38. the_pisano_period_of_nine_is_twenty_four_and_every_modulus_to_twelve_has_one — pisano 9 = 24 ∧ (List.range' 2 11).all (fun m => pisano m > 0 && fib (pisano m) % m == 0 && fib (pisano m + 1) % m == 1) record
  39. the_digit_sum_rules_for_three_and_nine_hold_below_ten_thousand — (List.range 100).all (fun a => (List.range 100).all (fun b => (digitSum (a * 100 + b) % 3 == 0) == ((a * 100 + b) % 3 == 0) && ((digitSum (a * 100 + b) % 9 == 0) == ((a * 100 + b) % 9 == 0)))) record
  40. the_involutions_are_counted_by_the_telephone_numbers — (List.range 6).all (fun n => ((permsN (List.range n)).filter isInvolution).length == telephone n) record
  41. invOf_is_an_inverse_and_an_involution_on_the_units — (List.range 9).all (fun d => match invOf d with | some e => d * e % 9 == 1 && invOf e == some d | none => gcd' d 9 != 1) record
  42. choose_is_invariant_under_the_involution_k_to_n_minus_k — (List.range 13).all (fun n => (List.range (n + 1)).all (fun k => choose n k == choose n (n - k) && n - (n - k) == k)) record
  43. the_powers_of_two_sum_to_one_less_than_the_next_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, ((List.range (n + 1)).map (fun i => 2 ^ i)).foldl (· + ·) 0 = 2 ^ (n + 1) - 1 record
  44. square_of_successor — ∀ n : Nat, (n + 1) * (n + 1) = n * n + 2 * n + 1 record
  45. the_first_n_odd_numbers_sum_to_n_squared_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, ((List.range n).map (fun i => 2 * i + 1)).foldl (· + ·) 0 = n * n record
  46. cassinis_identity_for_every_m — ∀ m : Nat, fib (2 * m + 1) * fib (2 * m + 3) = fib (2 * m + 2) * fib (2 * m + 2) + 1 ∧ fib (2 * m) * fib (2 * m + 2) + 1 = fib (2 * m + 1) * fib (2 * m + 1) record
  47. a_sum_over_one_to_n_plus_one_adds_the_last_term — ∀ (g : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat), ((List.range' 1 (n + 1)).map g).foldl (· + ·) 0 = ((List.range' 1 n).map g).foldl (· + ·) 0 + g (n + 1) record
  48. the_numbers_sum_to_their_closed_form_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, 2 * powSum 1 n = n * (n + 1) record
  49. the_squares_sum_to_their_closed_form_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, 6 * powSum 2 n = n * (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1) record
  50. the_cubes_sum_to_their_closed_form_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, 4 * powSum 3 n = n * n * (n + 1) * (n + 1) record
  51. the_fourth_powers_sum_to_their_closed_form_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, 30 * powSum 4 n = n * (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1) * (3 * n * n + 3 * n - 1) record
  52. the_fifth_powers_sum_to_their_closed_form_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, 12 * powSum 5 n = n * n * (n + 1) * (n + 1) * (2 * n * n + 2 * n - 1) record
  53. power_sums_match_their_closed_forms_for_every_n — ∀ k n : Nat, 1 ≤ k → k ≤ 5 → powSum k n = faulhaber k n record
  54. the_sums_of_triangular_numbers_are_the_tetrahedral_numbers_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, ((List.range' 1 n).map (fun i => i * (i + 1) / 2)).foldl (· + ·) 0 = n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) / 6 record
  55. choose_is_invariant_under_the_involution_k_to_n_minus_k_for_every_n — ∀ n k : Nat, k ≤ n → choose n k = choose n (n - k) ∧ n - (n - k) = k record
  56. the_closed_forms_difference_back_to_the_next_power_for_every_n — ∀ k n : Nat, 1 ≤ k → k ≤ 5 → faulhaber k (n + 1) = faulhaber k n + (n + 1) ^ k record

  59. the_odd_numbers_difference_back_to_the_next_odd_number_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, ((List.range (n + 1)).map (fun i => 2 * i + 1)).foldl (· + ·) 0 - ((List.range n).map (fun i => 2 * i + 1)).foldl (· + ·) 0 = 2 * n + 1 record
  60. foldl_add_start — ∀ (l : List Nat) (a : Nat), l.foldl (· + ·) a = a + l.foldl (· + ·) 0 record
  61. the_digits_sum_to_the_number_mod_nine_when_the_fuel_covers_them — ∀ f n : Nat, n < 10 ^ f → (digitsF f n).foldl (· + ·) 0 % 9 = n % 9 record
  62. a_number_is_below_ten_to_its_own_successor — ∀ n : Nat, n < 10 ^ (n + 1) record
  63. the_digit_sum_rules_for_three_and_nine_hold_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, (digitSum n % 3 = 0 ↔ n % 3 = 0) ∧ (digitSum n % 9 = 0 ↔ n % 9 = 0) record
